_comment: Canonical Claude Code tool deny list for the aetherclaude account.
This mirrors the --disallowedTools string in bin/run-agent.sh's
run_claude. That flag only covers the orchestrator; entrypoints that
invoke claude directly — run-stale-triage.sh, run-release-notes.sh —
each pass their own shorter list, so a tool denied for the orchestrator
was not necessarily denied for them. Landing the same set in the user
settings closes that gap: run_claude passes --setting-sources user, so
these denials apply to every claude invocation on this account, and
deny takes precedence over allow.
Deployed by scripts/deploy.sh via bin/sync-claude-settings.py, which
merges only the permissions.deny key and leaves the rest of
settings.json (model, effortLevel, hooks, env, theme, tui) untouched.
Keep in sync with run-agent.sh. The dashboard's Ring 5 posture check
counts these entries; an empty list reads as 'tool deny list not
loaded'.
The Bash(cat <path>) entries are necessary but nowhere near
sufficient on their own: they match one exact command string, and
head, tail, grep, od and a dozen other verbs read the same bytes.
The Read(...)/Edit(...) rules below are the ones that actually hold,
because they gate on the path rather than on how it is spelled.
